title: ClawMMU: Protection-Coherent Virtual Memory for Stateful LLM Agents

object.carrier: ClawVM-style typed memory pages: every representation of a page carries a protection descriptor (owner, scope, origins, authority level such as Evidence up to Policy) plus per-page revocation counters kept outside checkpoints

safety_property.statement: Information may rise in authority only through owner approval ('authority never lifts itself'): untrusted content (web pages, tool outputs, model-written summaries) can neither gain the user's authority nor supply security-relevant tool-call arguments, even when the model is fooled. Explicitly out of scope: confidentiality of readable content, correctness of derived memory, and the model making the right call when passed values do have enough authority. Judged by construction/argument, not by experiments (system not yet implemented).
safety_property.operationalized_as: Protection descriptors (owner/scope/origins/authority) checked by the harness at four context-boundary crossings - map (entry), derive (write to storage), reload (retrieval/checkpoint restore), authorize (tool call) - plus revocation-counter comparison at reload and authorize; violations surface as classical protection faults (address-space violation, type confusion, use-after-revoke, confused deputy). No implementation or measured numbers yet.

capabilities: Adversary controls text in fetched web pages and tool outputs that the agent retrieves, transforms, and stores
Sleeper memory poisoning: injected text is stored in memory and fires later, after passing through several summaries and transformations
Direct prompt injection by another user of a shared agent (same pattern, mentioned as in-scope motivation)
Adaptive attackers tuning inputs against a specific deployed defense (motivating content-independent checks)
assumptions: The harness is trusted; ClawMMU needs only a hook where content enters context, is written to storage, returns from storage, or drives a tool call
Stable page identities exist so every representation can be labeled
Current revocation counters are kept outside checkpoints so a restore cannot roll them back
Capability schemas are reviewed and correctly mark security-relevant arguments as checked
The model itself is treated as a lowest-authority input; only the owner can raise authority
not_covered: Model making the wrong call, or passing a wrong value that does have enough authority
A wrong 'safe' marking in a capability schema (stated as the main residual risk)
Actions that happen before a revocation
Authority in multi-agent systems and auditing approvals that widen scope (open problems)
No empirical evaluation yet; ClawMMU is not yet implemented

intervention.name: ClawMMU
intervention.description: An MMU-style protection layer in the agent harness: every memory representation carries a protection descriptor (owner, scope, origins, ordered authority levels with Evidence lowest and Policy highest); an inheritance rule gives derived memory the lowest authority of its inputs, counting the model itself as a lowest-authority input so model-written memory stays Evidence; per-page revocation counters (copied into descriptors of derived memory, kept outside checkpoints) invalidate all descendants of a revoked source; authorize performs per-argument checks so each security-relevant tool-call argument must trace to sufficient authority; compartment sharing across owners/scopes is denied by default via unforgeable assembly capabilities.

limitations.statement: ClawMMU's guarantee excludes correctness of the model's calls, correctness of derived memory, and confidentiality of readable content.
limitations.quote: It does not guarantee that the model makes the right call, that derived memory is correct, or that readable content stays confidential.

limitations.statement: Authorize protects only the provenance/integrity of call arguments; the model may still make the wrong call or pass a wrong value that has enough authority.
limitations.quote: The model may still make the wrong call, or pass a wrong value that does have enough authority.

limitations.statement: The main residual risk is a wrong 'safe' marking in a capability schema, so schemas must be reviewed.
limitations.quote: A wrong safe marking is therefore the main residual risk, which is why the schemas must be reviewed.

limitations.statement: ClawMMU is not yet implemented; its Table 1 row lists design properties only, and the planned evaluation (AgentDojo, InjecAgent, sleeper memory poisoning; attack success, check latency, owner approvals) is future work.
limitations.quote: The ClawMMU row lists design properties, since ClawMMU is not yet implemented.

limitations.statement: Open problems include capability-schema review at scale, authority in multi-agent systems, actions before a revocation, and auditing scope-widening approvals.
limitations.quote: Open problems include reviewing capability schemas at scale, placing authority in multi-agent systems, handling actions that happen before a revocation, and auditing approvals that widen scope.
